source_excerpts.text:
## 3. A condition-number-free N675 entropy filter

A second completed theorem strengthens the quantitative source machinery.

Suppose
\[
-h\rho\le H\le h\rho
\]
and two channels have a known positive SLD gap
\[
g^S_{\mathcal Q(\rho)}(\mathcal Q(H))
-
g^S_{\mathcal P(\rho)}(\mathcal P(H))
\ge d_0>0.
\]
Then the finite N675 resolvent filter constructs faithful state pairs with a computable positive Umegaki relative-entropy gap using flag size and constants depending only on \(h,d_0\). **No output condition-number bound is needed.**

The first new estimate is uniform over all positive eigenvalues \(a,b\):
\[
\left|
(a+b)\int\frac{\nu_m(dt)}{b+at}-1
\right|
\le3\sqrt{\frac2m}.
\]
Its key point is
\[
\left|\frac{a+b}{b+at}-1\right|
\le\frac{|1-t|}{t},
\]
combined with the reciprocal symmetry of the comparison beta-prime distribution. This avoids paying for an extreme eigenvalue ratio.

The second estimate controls noncommuting logarithm derivatives by a relative perturbation bound:
\[
-qS\le Y\le qS
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\left\|
\frac{d^k}{dt^k}\log(S+tY)\Big|_{t=0}
\right\|
\le k!q^k,\qquad k\ge2.
\]
Together, these yield explicit rational choices for the filter size, faithful mixing, perturbation amplitude, and final positive margin. The complete constants and proof are in the report. Both constructive collaborators independently checked the estimates and margin accounting.

This operation preserves the distinction you emphasized: the normalized N675 source already has its own dimension-independent scaled spectral bounds. The new theorem removes an additional conditioning dependence in this particular conversion; it does not replace the source bounds with a claim about an arbitrary channel’s \(\Phi(I)\).

Its remaining operational limitation is substantive. A finite filtered witness for each conditional state does not establish that **one fixed, physically paid sequential encoder** realizes those witnesses on every history.
